title: Establish per-endpoint Availability Index SLI and automated error-budget arbitration
creator: Aisha K. Romero
description: Define and implement a composite per-endpoint SLI called the 'Availability Index' (AI). AI combines three signals: request success rate (HTTP/ML-level success), latency tail (p99 latency with decay), and model-quality signal (automated promptset checks / quality probes). The index should be token-weighted, support per-variant weighting, and be calculable per-region and globally. Build an arbitration service that automatically reconciles error budget transfers between regions and model variants, and ties into circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shedding controllers to trigger graduated mitigations when AI approaches violation zones.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Availability Index computed for every endpoint and variant in production with hourly aggregates and 1m rolling windows
A2: Token-weighting implemented so long-running/high-token requests influence SLI proportionally
A3: Arbitration service can perform simulated transfers of error budget between two regions for a given endpoint and emit audit logs

A4: Circuit-breaker integration: when AI falls below warning threshold for 5m, system proposes staged mitigation (reduce variant weight, enable degrade policy); when below critical, it triggers automated eviction per policy
A5: Dashboards display AI, component SLI signals, per-variant contribution, and error-budget ledger with provenance
A6: End-to-end tests and canary rollout to a small set of low-risk endpoints with rollback on regressions
implementation_plan: Step 1: Finalize AI formula and per-signal weights with PM and SRE (latency, success, quality). Document in Confluence.
Step 2: Extend telemetry pipeline to emit token-count and variant-weighted request records. Add lightweight quality probe hooks into evaluation runner.
Step 3: Implement AI calculator as sidecar service with idempotent hourly aggregation and 1m rolling window streams.
Step 4: Build arbitration microservice that accepts transfer proposals, validates invariants, logs decisions, and exposes dry-run endpoint.
Step 5: Wire arbitration outputs into circuit-breaker manager and load-shedding controller with a policy layer (staged actions).
Step 6: Create dashboards, alerts, and runbook entries. Perform canary on 'dev' region then 'staging' then 5% production routes.
Step 7: Iterate thresholds after 2 weeks of telemetry and run synthetic stress tests.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Implement AI formula and telemetry changes behind feature flag; unit tests and CI checks.
Week 2: Deploy AI calculator to staging; validate against historical data (backfill) and compare with existing SLI baselines.
Week 3: Deploy arbitration service in dry-run mode in production; surface proposals to SRE dashboard (no automated changes).
Week 4: Enable automated arbitration for a single low-risk endpoint group with conservative thresholds and human approval hooks.
Week 6: Expand automated arbitration to additional endpoints; tune thresholds and add canary auto-rollbacks.
Week 8: Full production enablement for non-critical endpoints; schedule review for critical/enterprise routes with customers.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create Grafana dashboard 'AI / ErrorBudget Ledger' showing AI, success rate, p99 latency, quality probe score, per-variant contribution, and regional deltas.
Alert P0 when AI < critical_threshold for > 3m for a production route; page on-call SRE and open incident if arbitration recommended action != applied.
Alert P1 when AI < warning_threshold for > 10m; post to #reliability for manual review.
Emit structured audit events for every arbitration proposal/decision with provenance tags (caller, dry-run flag, reason, affected capacity).
Record latency-sensitive metrics for arbitration decisions to ensure decisions themselves do not increase system load.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Mis-calibrated AI weights could over-trigger evictions and cause unnecessary degradation. Mitigation: start conservative, dry-run mode, and run backfill comparisons against historical incidents.
Risk: Arbitration automation causes churn across regions (flip-flopping). Mitigation: add hysteresis, min-lease durations for transfers, and cooldown windows.
Risk: Increased telemetry volume from token-counts could raise cost. Mitigation: sample large requests, compress records, and use aggregated counters for high-volume routes.
Risk: Enterprise customers require explicit opt-in for automated mitigation. Mitigation: policy layer supports per-tenant opt-out and manual approval flows.
